name: Protocol-Faithful Analytics Command Queues
summary: Verify third-party analytics command payload shapes against the actual SDK protocol before mistaking a loaded library or consented page for delivered events.
problem: A custom gtag bootstrap can load the Google SDK successfully yet silently suppress collection when it enqueues rest-parameter arrays instead of the required Arguments command shape.
coreOutcomes: Command queue shape captured at its actual browser boundary
Correct Google gtag Arguments-object protocol in supported integrations
Consent/canonical-route admission kept separate from queue mechanics
SDK load, emitted network hit and destination ingestion tested independently
requirements: Access to the source of the public analytics bootstrap
Provider documentation for the exact current command protocol
A controlled browser/SDK test after valid visitor consent
An explicit privacy boundary and allowed public routes
boundaries: Do not change opt-in or opt-out privacy policies merely to increase hits
SDK HTTP 200 is not a collection receipt or conversion
Queue unit tests do not prove GA4 provider ingestion or reporting
Do not log personal data, private URLs or advertising identifiers
Do not copy an Arguments shim to unrelated SDKs without validating their contract
